To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatiotemporally transfer function of human reflex accommodation is best at 3-5 c/deg and that the profile of this function is not altered when the subject is instructed to focus on a dynamic blur stimulus.

the spatiotemporally tuned "reflex" accommodative mechanism is insensitive to temporal frequencies of target motion below 0.05 Hz and that the accommodative gain profile is not altered by the instruction at spatial frequencies of 3 and 10 c/deg.
reflex" accommodative responses to sinusoidal target motion are best at spatial frequencies of 3 and 4 c/deg at temporal frequencies of 0.1-0.5 Hz.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an understanding of the mechanisms of "reflex accommodation."

the control of accommodation in the presence of moving targets, the effect of spatial frequency of the target on the accommodative response and the role of voluntary and "reflex" components of accommodation.
the spatiotemporally dependent transfer function of human accommodative responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reflex" accommodative mechanisms are not well described by the fine focus control model.
the spatiotemporally tuned accommodative system does not appear to have the characteristics of the proposed mechanism or to support the fine focus control model.
the spatiotemporally selective accommodative responses are not due to a single "reflex" accommodative mechanism, but may be due to the combined effects of several different mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatiotemporally transfer function of "reflex accommodation is best described by a first-order system with a gain of approximately 0.4 and a time constant of 0.5 s.
the spatiotemporally tuned accommodative mechanism that has been proposed as the basis for the fine focus control of accommodation is not supported by these results.
the accommodative system does not respond in a linear fashion to sinusoidal motion of the accommodative blur target.

it is important to be careful about how we instruct subjects in dynamic accommodation experiments.
